newsitem.title: CUBA: Pope will visit Cuba in 1998, Cuban cardinal says.
newsitem.headline: Pope will visit Cuba in 1998, Cuban cardinal says.

text.p: Pope John Paul will make his planned trip to communist-ruled Cuba in January 1998, Cuban Cardinal Jaime Ortega said on Friday.

Ortega made the annoucement in a statement issued just before an evening Mass at Havana cathedral. The Mass was attended by the visiting president of Italy's Roman Catholic bishops' conference cardinal Camilo Ruini.

It was agreed that the Pope would make a trip to Cuba, the only Spanish-speaking Latin American country he has not visited, at an historic first meeting between the pontiff and President Fidel Castro at the Vatican last November.
A date had not been announced, although the Vatican initially said the trip would take place during 1997.

The later date appeared to be at least in part because the 76-year-old pontiff already has several other foreign trips planned for 1997, and because since surgery to remove his appendix last year, he has been told by doctors to reduce his workload.

The meeting between Castro and the Pope, and the announcement that the Pope would visit Cuba marked a clear improvement in recent months in ties between Cuba's communist authorities and the Roman Catholic church.
